# Test Performance of Intel-Optimized Libraries

The idea here is to analyze whether there is any speed gain from using the Intel-optimized
python libraries instead of the base conda-forge versions. I expect the benefit will be 
greatest for the matrix multiplactions because the libraries specifically focus on numpy
and scipy functionality. 

### 1) Load in Libraries and Set global Variables

```{r} 
#Call needed libraries
library(tidyverse)

#Set file paths of intel-optimized and conda-forge test log files
intel_optimized_path <- "C:/Users/mconery/Box/Mitchell_Work_Files/Meta-Analysis_Fine-Mapping/Data/Aurora_Timing_Test/multinode_1000G_test.intel_version.log"
conda_forge_path <- "C:/Users/mconery/Box/Mitchell_Work_Files/Meta-Analysis_Fine-Mapping/Data/Aurora_Timing_Test/multinode_1000G_test.nonopt_version.log"

```

### 2) Extract Completion Times and Plot Results

```{r}
#Create a function to extract completion times
# Define the function
extract_completion_times <- function(file_path) {
  # Read the log file into a vector of lines
  log_lines <- readLines(file_path)
  
  # Use a regular expression to match lines with the desired format
  success_lines <- grep("SUCCESS: Simulation complete in [0-9\\.]+ seconds", log_lines, value = TRUE)
  
  # Extract the numeric completion times from the matched lines
  completion_times <- as.numeric(sub(".*SUCCESS: Simulation complete in ([0-9\\.]+) seconds.*", "\\1", success_lines))
  
  # Return the vector of completion times
  return(completion_times)
}

# Extract completion times
intel_optimized_completion_times <- extract_completion_times(intel_optimized_path)
conda_forge_completion_times <- extract_completion_times(conda_forge_path)

#Combine vectors into a dataframe
lcf_completed_tasks = min(length(intel_optimized_completion_times),length(conda_forge_completion_times))
completion_times_df <- cbind.data.frame(library_type=c(rep("Intel-Optimized", lcf_completed_tasks), rep("Conda-Forge", lcf_completed_tasks)), 
                                        completion_times=c(intel_optimized_completion_times[1:lcf_completed_tasks],conda_forge_completion_times[1:lcf_completed_tasks]),
                                        task_number=rep(paste0("task_",seq(1,lcf_completed_tasks,1)),2))

ggplot(completion_times_df, aes(x = library_type, y = completion_times)) + 
geom_boxplot(aes(fill = library_type), alpha = .2) +
geom_line(aes(group = task_number)) + 
geom_point(size = 2)  + ylab('Completion Time') +
  theme(panel.background = element_blank(), legend.title = element_blank(), axis.line = element_line(colour = "black"),
          plot.title = element_text(size=20, color="black", hjust=0.5), axis.title.x = element_blank(),
          legend.position = "none", axis.text = element_text(size=12), axis.title.y = element_text(size = 16))

```
